Language of the settings screen and of the keyboard\'s own texts.

Chooses the language of this screen and of the messages shown by the keyboard. \"System language\" follows your phone and is the default. This only changes the interface: the languages you type in are set under \"Languages\". On Android 13 and later, the choice is also available in the system settings, under the language of each app.
AZERTY or QWERTY key arrangement.

Chooses the arrangement of the letter keys. By default it follows the system language: AZERTY if it is French, QWERTY otherwise. The layout does not depend on the language you type in, so a French speaker who writes English keeps their AZERTY. The change applies at once.
How much the keys change with the letters that are likely next.

After each keystroke the keyboard estimates which letters are likely next and shows them more clearly. Off: nothing moves. Calm: likely letters are only more opaque, the others fainter. Reinforced calm (default): in addition, a slight change of label size and key width, kept small. Elastic: the strongest effect, with larger changes of size and width. A faded key can always be pressed normally. With TalkBack on, the keyboard keeps its resting layout.
Height of the key rows, from 34 to 46 dp.

Sets the height of each row of keys, from 34 to 46 dp (default: 38 dp). Taller rows are easier to hit but take more room on the screen; shorter rows leave more of the app visible. The change applies at once.
Extra space under the last row, from 0 to 48 dp.

Adds blank space under the last row, on top of the space the keyboard already leaves for the system navigation bar. It raises the keyboard above the system buttons if you tend to press them by mistake. From 0 to 48 dp (default: 0 dp, no extra space).

On screens at least 400 dp wide, makes the \?123 (or ABC), ↵ and ⌫ keys narrower so that the space bar is wider and easier to hit. It has no effect on narrower screens, in password fields, on the classic layout or on the numeric pads. Default: off.
Strength of the vibration when you press a key.

Chooses how strongly the phone vibrates when you press a key: off, light, medium (default) or strong. The keyboard uses the system\'s haptic feedback, so nothing happens if \"Touch feedback\" (or vibration on touch) is turned off in the Android settings.
Languages the keyboard predicts and corrects in.

Chooses the languages used for suggestions and corrections: French, English, or both (default). With both, you never need to switch: the keyboard follows the language of the words you type, even within one sentence. Choosing one language removes the other from suggestions, which can avoid mix-ups if you only write in one.
Language assumed when you start typing, before any word.

Sets the language the keyboard assumes at first, before it has seen any word you typed. It then adapts to your words. By default it follows the system language, provided that language is active; otherwise the first active language is used. It only matters when both languages are active.

When you press the space bar, the keyboard completes or corrects the word if one candidate clearly dominates (for example \"bonjoru\" becomes \"bonjour\"), and the space key then shows the word it will insert. Pressing ⌫ just after cancels the change and restores what you typed. A correction you cancel twice is no longer applied automatically. It is never applied in password, e-mail, URL or numeric fields. Default: on.
How sure the keyboard must be before it replaces a word.

Sets how certain a candidate must be for the space bar to replace what you typed, and how far ahead of the second candidate it must be. To judge a typo, the keyboard takes into account exactly where your finger landed, kept in memory for the current word only. Cautious: rarely replaces, fewest wrong replacements. Normal (default): in simulations with 5 percent typos, at most about 2 percent of the words were wrongly replaced. Bold: replaces more often, at the cost of more mistakes. It only applies if \"Commit on space\" is on, and suggestions stay available in the bar whatever you choose.

When you type in French, inserts a non-breaking space before ; ! ? and :, and inside « » quotes, as French typography requires, so that the sign never ends up alone at the start of a line. It only applies to sentences detected as French, never to English ones. Default: on.
Pressing the space bar twice replaces the space by a period followed by a space, and the next word starts with a capital letter if the field allows it. Default: on.

Lets the keyboard suggest the first names, last names and nicknames from your address book, mainly after words such as \"hello\" or \"with\", or in name fields. It needs the contacts permission, requested when you turn this on. Names are read each time the keyboard starts or your contacts change, kept in memory only, never written to storage and never sent anywhere (Nextglyph has no network access). Turning this off, or removing the permission, erases them at once. Default: off.
Words and habits the keyboard has learned from you.

The keyboard learns the unknown words you type (after two validations without cancelling), the corrections you reject and how your fingers land on the keys. Nothing is learned in incognito mode, password, e-mail, URL or numeric fields. This data stays in the app\'s private storage and is excluded from backups. You can export the learned words to a TSV file, import such a file, or erase everything with one tap, after confirmation.
Counters of your typing, kept on this device.

Shows your typing speed, how often you press ⌫, how many words the keyboard completed or corrected, how many automatic corrections and restored accents or capitals you cancelled, and the cancellation rate for each prudence level. Cancelling a replacement is not counted as a ⌫ press. They help you judge how well the keyboard suits you. Only counters are kept, never any text, and nothing is counted in incognito mode or in password, e-mail, URL or numeric fields. Nothing leaves the device. You can reset them at any time.
Refused corrections
Corrections you undid twice, which the keyboard no longer applies.

When you undo the same automatic correction twice, the keyboard stops applying it and the word you typed joins your personal dictionary. Here you can see these refusals and remove some: the word then leaves your personal dictionary and the keyboard may correct it again. Only the typed word and its correction are kept, on this device only, never any context.
See refused corrections
Touch zones
Where your fingers actually land on each key.

The keyboard learns where you actually tap on each letter, and on space, ↵, ⌫ and \?123, from the taps you do not correct. It then slightly and invisibly shifts each key\'s zone: if you often aim a little left of the space bar, the space bar grows on that side, by at most a fifth of a key. Suggestions never take part in this choice. The number shown counts the taps kept (at most the 300 most recent per key). Nothing is learned in incognito mode or in password or numeric fields. \"Erase learned data\" restores the original zones.
